title: Cedar Ridge Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Cedar Ridge Health onboarding to Redwood. Reviewed account goals (patient triage automation + internal QA), onboarding timeline, integration options (hosted API vs private VPC), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), success criteria for pilot, and immediate next steps around security docs, SSO onboarding, and a 2-week technical deep dive to run benchmarks.

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood - I'm the account lead. We've got Samir our SE and Elena from CS on. Quick intros?
[00:12] Maya Torres: Hi I'm Maya, head of engineering at Cedar Ridge. We're running provider platform for scheduling and patient intake.
[00:22] Ibrahim Khan: Ibrahim here, platform lead, I'll own infra.
[00:28] Elena Morris: Elena from CSM, I'll coordinate the onboarding timeline.
[00:34] Jordan Lee: Great, goal for today is align on pilot success criteria and next steps. High level, you mentioned patient triage and QA automation as use cases?
[00:45] Maya Torres: Yes, exactly. We want to automate triage to reduce phone volume and also have a model check for clinician notes for consistency. Both need low latency for triage, accuracy is critical for QA.
[01:02] Samir Gupta: Quick question on latency targets — what's acceptable?
[01:06] Dr. Aaron Patel: For triage we want sub-500ms median ideally, 95th under 1s. For QA batch jobs can be slower.
[01:15] Samir Gupta: Okay that's helpful. Hosted API can hit low latency depending on routing and model, but for tight SLOs Dedicated or Private with reserved GPUs gives better predictability.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: Security is a hard requirement — we need SOC2 compliance, audit logs, SSO, and KMS for key management. Data residency is also something to confirm.
[01:43] Jordan Lee: We're SOC2 compliant and have KMS integrations; Samir will share the security pack after this call. For residency, we have regions in US-East and US-West, and Private deployment allows on-prem or VPC if you need full isolation.
[01:58] Ibrahim Khan: If we go Private, what's the ops overhead? We want minimal ops touch but strict isolation.
[02:04] Samir Gupta: Private involves customer-managed networking and an installer; Redwood control plane can be run in a customer VPC. There is more setup up front but lower maintenance afterwards; we also offer Dedicated which is a middle ground — reserved capacity but still managed by Redwood.
[02:22] Maya Torres: Cost is a concern; what are the tradeoffs?
[02:26] Jordan Lee: Roughly, hosted pay-as-you-go is lowest startup cost; Dedicated has predictable monthly commits; Private has licensing and support fees. We'll include cost examples in the SOW.
[02:38] Dr. Aaron Patel: For the pilot, what success metrics would you recommend?
[02:42] Samir Gupta: I'd propose: 1) triage accuracy within X% of current baseline on our eval set, 2) median latency target <500ms on the chosen infra, 3) cost per 1k requests under agreed threshold, 4) integration readiness (SSO + logs).
[02:58] Maya Torres: Sounds good. We'll provide baseline metrics.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: Great, timeline — target 6 week pilot: week 1 onboarding + infra, week 2-3 integration and sample run, week 4 benchmark and tuning, week 5-6 pilot evaluation and wrap. Does that align?
[03:18] Ibrahim Khan: That works if we can allocate one infra engineer for weeks 1-3.
[03:23] Elena Morris: We'll draft timeline and resource needs after call.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: Okay, technical items: API keys, SDKs, sample prompts, and a checklist for SSO and KMS. Samir, can you run through the typical integration steps?
[03:40] Samir Gupta: Sure — step 1: create trial account or OBO token for test, step 2: decide hosted vs private, step 3: if private, exchange VPC peering / CIDR and firewall rules, step 4: configure SAML SSO and test, step 5: share sample prompt set and evaluation harness, step 6: run benchmarks and profiling.
[03:58] Maya Torres: For SSO we use Okta. What's required?
[04:02] Samir Gupta: We'll need SAML metadata and a test user. We support automatic provisioning via SCIM if you want.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: For audit logs we need retention 7 years for some clinical logs; is that supported?
[04:16] Elena Morris: Audit log retention is an add-on — we can configure long-term retention and export to your log bucket; Samir will include options.
[04:26] Ibrahim Khan: About encryption — we need customer-managed keys, HSM if possible.
[04:31] Samir Gupta: We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys (CMK); HSM-based key storage can be part of Private deployments. I'll include specifics in the security docs.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: Any blockers on compliance from your side?
[04:47] Lena Ortiz: We need a vendor questionnaire answered and the SOC2 report.
[04:51] Jordan Lee: We'll send that right after this call.
[05:00] Maya Torres: For benchmarks, we have a dataset of anonymized chats and clinician notes; how do you prefer delivery?
[05:07] Samir Gupta: S3 or secure upload links work. Please redact PII — anonymized is best. We'll run the workload against a couple model variants and a dedicated instance for throughput numbers.
[05:21] Jordan Lee: Competitor question — we evaluated ProviderX and OpenAI; any noteworthy differences?
[05:26] Samir Gupta: Main differences are control and economics: Redwood emphasizes predictable serving, batching, and cost controls; other providers are more black-box. For private deployments we offer more control than typical hosted-only vendors.
[05:39] Dr. Aaron Patel: Ok two practical asks: can you run an initial latency benchmark with our sample prompts and show token-level cost breakdown?
[05:47] Samir Gupta: Yes — that's part of the SE-led benchmark. We'll produce latency p50/p95, token breakdown, and suggestions (batching/quantization).
[05:55] Jordan Lee: Logistics — I'll send SOW and pricing. Elena will coordinate internal kickoff calendar.
[06:02] Elena Morris: I'll set up the follow-up meeting for the technical deep dive.
[06:07] Maya Torres: Who should I send the dataset to?
[06:10] Samir Gupta: Send to samir@redwood.ai secure link or we can provide an upload URL; we'll confirm in the security pack.
[06:18] Ibrahim Khan: For private deployment, how long does provisioning take?
[06:21] Samir Gupta: Typical private deployment setup is 2-4 weeks depending on network approvals; Dedicated can be turned on faster if you're okay with upstream-managed infra.
[06:32] Jordan Lee: Any contractual constraints — procurement/legal items?
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: We'll need insurance certs, DPA, and an execution-ready SOW. Procurement will review SLAs.
[06:44] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll add those to the SOW.
[06:49] Maya Torres: On ownership — how are model outputs handled for IP?
[06:53] Jordan Lee: Redwood's standard terms grant you ownership of your data and outputs; we'll detail in the contract and SOW.
[07:01] Samir Gupta: If you're doing local model tuning, that can change IP terms; we'll flag that in the SOW.
[07:08] Elena Morris: Next we'll confirm pilot goals and owners — Jordan to own the SOW, Samir to own technical run, Elena to coordinate schedule, Maya/Ibrahim to provide data and infra.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: Quick recap of next steps: security pack, SOW, sample prompts, SSO metadata, schedule deep-dive. Any other questions?
[07:34] Maya Torres: No, looks good. Thanks all.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: Thanks everybody — we'll follow up by end of week.
[07:42] *call ends*
